# INC-5521: Oversold stock and stuck holds during the September flash sale

Reported by the checkout team after the 2026-09-12 flash sale.

## What we saw

- The `sneaker-limited` drop had 250 units. We confirmed 263 orders, and 13
  customers had to be refunded.
- The stock dashboard showed `reserved` going negative for two SKUs after the
  sale, and it has not recovered.
- Some customers who retried checkout after a timeout had units held twice for
  one order; the second hold only disappeared when the reservation expired.
- One order was rejected because a bundle item was out of stock, but the other
  item in the bundle stayed held until we restarted the worker pool.
- Finance reports `sold` counts that are higher than the number of orders we
  shipped for a few SKUs.

## Context

Every checkout worker calls `InventoryService` concurrently. During the sale
we ran 40 workers. The nightly `expire()` job ran once during the sale.

The unit tests all pass, and none of this reproduces when we click through
checkout by hand.

A service-wide lock (INC-5490) stopped the overselling in staging but cut
checkout throughput by 90% and was rolled back the same day.

I've fixed every problem in the incident report, and each one has a test that reproduces it. The full suite passes: 38 of 38, run through `dx run-gate --name full-gate`. Before the fix, 26 of the 27 new service tests failed on the old code, and the one that passed is a TTL boundary guard for the rewritten `expire()`.

## What caused each symptom

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| 263 orders for 250 units | `reserve`, `commit` and `addStock` read a SKU record, change it and write it back with no lock. Concurrent callers all read the same value, so updates to `reserved` and `stock` were lost. |
| `reserved` negative | `release()` didn't refuse committed orders, even though its doc comment says it must. `expire()` released anything older than the TTL whatever its status, so the one sweep during the sale released committed orders and subtracted their units from `reserved` a second time. Racing releases and commits on one order also both ran. |
| Double hold on a retry | The check for an existing order and the write of the new one weren't atomic. A retry that arrived while the first attempt was still running found no order and held the stock again. The extra hold "disappeared at expiry" only because `expire()` then wrongly released the committed order, which cancelled it out. |
| Bundle item stayed held | `reserve` held items one at a time and threw on a later item without undoing the earlier ones. An unknown SKU later in the bundle did the same. |
| `sold` higher than orders shipped | Commit retries racing each other both added to `sold`. `expire()` also flipped committed orders to `released`, so they were counted as sold but never shipped. |

## The fix
- **Per-key locks (`src/keyed-lock.js`):** each call locks only the order and the SKUs it changes. It always takes the order's lock before any SKU lock, and SKU locks in sorted order, so bundles can't deadlock. There's no service-wide lock: a test checks that calls on other SKUs finish while one SKU's store calls are blocked. A lock entry exists only while it's held, so memory doesn't grow with the number of SKUs.
- **`reserve`:** it checks the existing order under the order's lock, so a retry waits for the attempt in flight and returns its reservation. It checks every item before writing any, and copies the `items` array before its first `await`.
- **`release`:** a committed order now throws `OrderStateError`. Callers that used to get a silent "success" here will now get that error.
- **`expire()`:** it rechecks each order's status under that order's lock and returns only the orders it actually released.
- `src/store.js`, the error classes and the public methods are unchanged.

## Tests
- **`tests/inc-5521.test.js`:** one group per symptom. It also covers 40 workers that each build their own service over one store, the lock-scope and deadlock checks, and a seeded random workload that checks the counters against the order records.
- **`tests/keyed-lock.test.js`:** checks that the lock hands over in arrival order, releases when the callback throws, and drops keys once no one holds them.
- **Checking the tests:** I reintroduced each defect one at a time in a throwaway copy of the repo, and every one made at least one test fail.

## Assumptions and limits
- **Workers share a process.** The locks are shared by every service built on the same store object, but they don't reach across processes. If the 40 workers are separate processes on one Redis, you need atomic operations in the store (a Lua script, or WATCH/MULTI), which `get`/`set`/`keys` can't provide.
- **Not handled, possible follow-ups:**
  - If the store fails partway through writing a bundle, the counters are left half-updated, because the store has no multi-key transaction.
  - Store calls have no timeouts, so a hung call keeps its keys locked.
- **No `destroy()` or README:** the lock uses no timers and cleans up after itself, and this is an existing project rather than a new library.
- **Not committed:** you didn't ask for a commit and there's no remote, so the changes are uncommitted in the working tree.
